payload.learnerResponse: The move from B to C is a plan for TRN102, not a received confirmation that it has happened. Accordingly, Stand B is not confirmed available yet. I would keep the planned move and the stand-availability update separate when describing this checkpoint. The first concerns an intended reposition, while the second would establish that the resource is free; the reports here have not supplied that second confirmation. That leaves availability unresolved at this cutoff, rather than establishing either that the stand has become available or that the proposed move itself is an availability report.

payload.learnerResponse: I cannot establish overall departure readiness from these reports. They tell us fuel service and baggage loading are complete for TRN102 and its exercise ground hold is released. Those are the received updates, but they do not establish every prerequisite for departure and they do not grant permission to take off. My uncertainty is about what the reports establish: I am not claiming that the aircraft has failed a readiness check, or that a clearance has been refused. Service completion and a ground-hold release therefore leave the overall readiness question unresolved here.
